newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates dip on surplus stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates dip on surplus stocks.

text.p: Pakistan cotton prices dipped on Tuesday as ginners tried to unload surplus stocks from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop before the new crop arrives, dealers said.
"The arrival of the 1997/98 crop is due in the market in mid-June which has put ginners under pressure as they still have large quantities of surplus cotton," dealer Nasim Usman said.
Ginners hold more than 850,000 unsold bales, dealers said.
Dealer Khushi Ram said the overhang from this year's crop would put pressure on the prices of new cotton.
Dealers reported select buying from exporters, but mill owners stayed out because they were short of funds.
The kerb rate for NIAB-78 was around 1,750 ($43.28) rupees per maund (37.32 k.g.) and for K-68 around 2,000 rupees.
